findings.claim: HalıSaha+ already ships Avenza's entire stated differentiator — an attendance-reliability score, level-based matching, per-person payment split and post-match player rating — and explicitly names Kadıköy as a covered district.
findings.evidence: iTunes lookup API (id=6761794919, country=tr, fetched 2026-09-01; version 1.1.6, updated 2026-08-31) returns a description with a dedicated section: "GÜVEN PUANI — MAÇ İPTALİ DERDİ BİTSİN • Halı Saha+ Güven Puanı, maçı satıp ekibi yarı yolda bırakanları filtreler • Her oyuncunun katılım güvenilirliği profilinde görünür • Söz veren sahaya gelir" ("Trust Score — end the match-cancellation problem: it filters out those who sell the match and leave the squad stranded; every player's attendance reliability is visible on their profile"). Same description: "Mevkini, seviyeni, ilçeni ve boş saatlerini seç • Yapay zekâ seni performans puanına ve oyun sertliğine göre en dengeli maça yerleştirir" and "iyzico ile kredi kartı veya havale/EFT — herkes kendi payını öder" and "maç sonrası oyuncu değerlendirme". Corroborated on the vendor's own site: halisahaplus.com/tr/features states "İlçe, uygun saat ve seviye seç; sistem seni kadrosu dolu, dengeli bir maça eşleştirsin" under a "Güven & itibar" section listing "Oyuncu değerlendirmesi" and "Maç performans puanı", plus "Kaptan hepsini öder, herkes kendi payını öder ya da iki kaptan paylaşır". The homepage lists levels as four tiers (Başlangıç/Orta/İyi/Rekabetçi) and names Kadıköy, Beşiktaş, Çankaya among its districts. No commission percentage was disclosed anywhere on the site (homepage, /tr/features, /tr/faq all checked).
findings.consequence: The verbatim bet — "Nobody else knows whether the stranger you matched with will actually turn up, or is really the level they claim" — is false as written for football in Kadıköy as of 31 Aug 2026. RELIABILITY (the % attendance score) and the LEVEL-range match are not novel; a competitor is shipping both plus the piece Avenza deferred (real iyzico money movement with per-person split). Avenza should stop positioning the trust layer as the differentiator and re-anchor on what HalıSaha+ does not do: it is football-only, whereas Avenza's LEVEL is per-sport across eight sports and its VENUE pages and BULLETIN are cross-sport. Also note HalıSaha+ shows level as four coarse self-selected tiers, not a 1.0–7.0 number.

findings.claim: No one in the Turkish halı saha app market has distribution: all 17 apps launched in 2025–26 have 26 or fewer App Store TR ratings each and 167 ratings between them, fewer than the single abandoned incumbent Halısahavar's 154.
findings.evidence: iTunes search API (term=halısaha, entity=software, country=tr, limit=25, fetched 2026-09-01) returned 25 results; excluding 3 non-Turkish lineup apps leaves 22. Of those, 17 first released in 2025 or 2026. Every one has userRatingCount ≤ 26 (max: Altıpas 26 and Saha Bul 26; HalıSaha+ 18; Maçla 17; Santra 13; Pasona 11), summing to 167 across all 17. Halısahavar (id 1583998724) has 154 ratings at 4.60 but its iOS version 1.2.4 was last updated 2022-06-29 and its Android build was last updated "29 Ara 2021" (scraped from the Google Play TR page for com.halisahavarapp.halisahavar). The only three apps reaching Google Play's "10 B+" (10,000+) install bucket are Halısahavar (dead since Dec 2021), Adam Eksik (adam.eksik, 3.94 from 121 ratings, last updated 12 Eki 2024) and Altıpas. Santra's Play listing shows only "50+" installs despite shipping 23 Ağu 2026.
findings.consequence: The moat is liquidity in one district, not the trust layer — everyone has features, nobody has players. This makes Avenza's ELIGIBILITY rule its single biggest product risk: hard-filtering a game out of Discover and Search when the level range excludes you removes inventory from a feed that will start near-empty in Kadıköy. At competitor densities (tens of active users), a level-filtered Discover shows a new user nothing and they churn before the loop ever reaches Play->Rate->Reputation. Recommend the host's "let others ask anyway" opt-in be defaulted ON, or the filter be softened to a demotion rather than a hard hide, until a district has enough concurrent games to survive filtering.

findings.claim: The WhatsApp-group-and-missing-players problem that Avenza's ad concept names is now the explicit marketing hook of at least two live competitors, and the 2026 answer is WhatsApp interop plus no-account joining — not replacing the group chat.
findings.evidence: Santra's App Store TR description (id 6757343159, v1.8.0, updated 2026-08-24) opens verbatim: "Halı saha maçı ayarlamak, WhatsApp grubunda 'kim var, kim yok' mesajlarında kaybolmasın." Altıpas's release notes for v2.1.0 (updated 2026-08-27) lead with: "WhatsApp kadronu yapıştır: kadron ve dizilişin saniyeler içinde hazır olsun. Maçını linkle paylaş, uygulamada olmayan arkadaşların da kadrodan yer alsın", and its description adds "UYGULAMADA OLMAYAN ARKADAŞLARIN İÇİN — Maç bağlantısını paylaş; arkadaşların uygulamayı indirmeden linke tıklayıp kadrodaki yerini alsın." By contrast the oldest and largest player-finding incumbent, Adam Eksik (Play since 2 Ara 2019, 10 B+ installs, 121 ratings, last updated Oct 2024), still hands off out of the app: its Play page states "oyuncu profil bilgileri kısmından mobil numarasından ulaşarak maçınıza davet edebilirsiniz" (invite them by reaching them on their mobile number), and adameksik.com is a forum with threads like "Adana maç arıyorum". A Turkish 2026 directory of halı saha player/opponent WhatsApp groups is still being published (gruplari.com.tr).
findings.consequence: Avenza's ad concept is no longer a wedge; it is the category's shared pitch line. Two concrete gaps this opens in Avenza's own flows: (1) CREATE has no import path — Altıpas turns a pasted WhatsApp roster into a squad in seconds, which is how it seeds a game with real people rather than strangers; (2) ONBOARDING's deferred-signup / Google-Apple-only design is directionally correct but stops short of Altıpas's install-free link join, so a host who fills 6 of 10 spots from their existing group still has to make four friends install Avenza. Adding roster import and a web link-join to CREATE is a cheaper liquidity mechanism than the trust layer.

findings.claim: Every Turkish halı saha competitor exposes skill as a visible coarse label the player picks or earns, and none hides matches from a player because of it — Avenza's hidden 1.0–7.0 number combined with silent filtering is unique in this market and untested on Turkish players.
findings.evidence: Three distinct display conventions, all read from App Store TR descriptions fetched via the iTunes lookup API on 2026-09-01. HalıSaha+ (id 6761794919): four self-selected tiers, "Mevkini, seviyeni, ilçeni ve boş saatlerini seç", listed on halisahaplus.com as Başlangıç/Orta/İyi/Rekabetçi — the player declares level, the system then places them ("seni ... en dengeli maça yerleştirir"), it does not hide games. Santra (id 6757343159): a FIFA-style earned card, "Hız, şut, pas, dribling, defans, fizik - 6 yetenek kategorisi" and "Oyuncu yetenek kartı: Bronz → Gümüş → Altın → Elmas", plus "Fair play puanıyla centilmenliğini göster". Altıpas (id 6761342905): "Her maç sonrası yapılan değerlendirmelerle gelişen bir oyuncu kartın oluşur. Maç sayısı, galibiyet, gol, asist ve MVP oyların profilinde birikir; topluluk sıralamasında yüksel." Halısahavar (dead, but 154 ratings) used "HALISAHAVAR KARTINI OLUŞTUR! Mevkini seç, özelliklerini belirle". No description among the 22 Turkish apps examined describes suppressing or hiding matches on the basis of a player's level.
findings.consequence: Bears directly on LEVEL and ELIGIBILITY. Two implications. First, the market's convention is that level is a badge you show off and grow (bronze to diamond, MVP votes, community ranking) — a motivational surface. Avenza stores 1.0–7.0, matches on the number, displays 1–5 stars, and uses it destructively: it removes games from view. A player who cannot see what they were excluded from cannot understand or contest the number, which is the opposite of the reputation-as-reward loop competitors are building. Second, if Avenza keeps the hard filter it should at minimum surface the count of hidden games and the reason ("3 games near you need level 4+"), which preserves the filter's matching benefit while giving the LEVEL number a visible payoff and a reason to play again.

findings.claim: Playtomic's player level runs 0 to 7 per sport and its profile already shows a percentage labelled "reliability" — so Avenza's 1.0-7.0 level AND its "reliability %" are both direct collisions with the category leader's existing vocabulary, with reliability meaning two completely different things.
findings.evidence: Fetched Playtomic's own help centre with curl (WebFetch was blocked 403 by their bot filter). Article 19831827459345 states verbatim: "The Playtomic levels range from 0 to 7." Article 19831576375313 ("What does each section of the Playtomic player profile represent?") states verbatim: "The percentage of the reliability represents how reliable your level is. This is used to adjust your level after playing a match - the lower the percentage, the more it varies." Article 43310980754193 confirms the pipeline is questionnaire-seeded then match-derived: "This initial assessment can only be completed once and gives you your starting level", then level updates on match result, opponent levels, partner level, and "Your reliability score". It also confirms per-sport scope ("padel, tennis and pickleball") and that reliability "is set automatically by the system - neither you nor Playtomic Customer Care can adjust it manually", with a certified leveling session setting it to "medium (50%)". Article 19831855406609 confirms peer ratings already nudge level: "You need to receive a sufficient number of positive reviews from opponents you've played against... the level can increase by up to 0.5 points."
findings.consequence: Two of Avenza's three headline mechanics are pre-owned. (1) LEVEL: Avenza's 1.0-7.0 overlaps six of Playtomic's seven points, and Playtomic's version is per-sport, questionnaire-seeded, match-derived and peer-review-nudged — exactly Avenza's Rate -> Reputation -> better-matches loop, already shipped. Avenza displaying it as 1-5 stars while storing 1.0-7.0 is the only real divergence, and it is a lossy one: a Playtomic user who reads their own level as "3.25" gets a coarser number in Avenza. (2) RELIABILITY: Avenza puts a percentage on the profile next to a level and means attendance; Playtomic puts a percentage on the profile next to a level and means confidence-in-level. Any padel player arriving from Playtomic will misread Avenza's 94%. Avenza should either rename the mechanic ("Attendance", "Katılım") or explicitly contrast it in-product — the current label is the incumbent's word for something else.

findings.claim: Playtomic does NOT hide out-of-level open matches — it shows them, labels them "Out of range", and always offers a "Request a spot" path requiring unanimous approval from every already-enrolled player. Avenza's default (filter ineligible games out of Discover and Search entirely, host opt-in off) is strictly more restrictive than the category leader's.
findings.evidence: Fetched article 19832027031569 by curl. Verbatim: "If you want to join an open match but you don't have the required level for that match, you can 'Request a spot' to be included, even if you couldn't join due to level and accuracy restrictions." And from its FAQ block: "'Registration requirements not met' or 'Out of range' message: This means the match level is outside your current level range. You can still send a spot request - the existing players will be notified and can choose to accept you despite the level difference." The approval rule is unanimous and one-vote-vetoed: "The player who wants to join the match must be accepted by all of the other players who joined previously. However, it is enough for one player to reject the requested in order to not be accepted." Rejections are also reversible via a "Requests for places" list.
findings.consequence: Directly contradicts Avenza's ELIGIBILITY design. The incumbent that has the most level data and the most liquidity still chose to show ineligible matches, because hiding supply from a user with nothing else to look at is a churn event. Avenza will launch in one district of one city with a fraction of Playtomic's supply, so a hard filter empties Discover far faster. Two concrete moves: flip the host's "let others ask anyway" default to ON, and replace hard hiding with Playtomic's pattern — render the game, badge it "Seviye dışı / Out of range", and route to a request. Also note Playtomic's approval is unanimous-with-veto, not host-only; Avenza's host-only ask is a weaker social filter and worth reconsidering, since the existing players are the ones who bear a mismatched fourth.

findings.claim: Playtomic is effectively absent from Turkey — no Turkish localisation, 188 Turkish ratings against 75,597 in Spain, no Turkey in its published fee schedule, and zero Turkish clubs in a 140-club random sample of its 6,879-club sitemap — but at least three Turkey-built racquet apps already ship level-matching plus open matches plus cost-splitting, so Avenza's LEVEL mechanic is not a differentiator in Istanbul.
findings.evidence: Apple's keyless API (itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=1242321076) across nine storefronts: TR 188 ratings vs ES 75,597, IT 39,943, GB 33,040, DE 13,393, SE 12,054, NL 10,752. languageCodesISO2A = ['CA','DA','NL','EN','FI','FR','DE','IT','NB','PL','PT','ES','SV'] — 13 languages, no TR. Pulled playtomic.com/sitemap.xml: locale prefixes are es/it/pt/fi/sv/nl/fr/de only, no /tr/; 61,911 URLs resolve to 6,879 unique clubs. Fetched 140 randomly sampled club pages concurrently and parsed the meta description ("Welcome to X, in <city>") — 0 Turkish cities (top hits Roma, Madrid, Zapopan, Centurion, Dubai). sitemap-pages.xml has 26 padel-courts and 26 tennis-courts city landing pages including Doha, Dubai, Singapore, Cape Town, Nicosia, Tijuana — none Turkish. The Service Fee article lists 36 countries; Türkiye is not among them. Against that, the TR App Store returns Turkey-built rivals whose own descriptions claim the mechanic: Matchabit (36 TR ratings) — "an advanced leveling system that adjusts based on match outcomes", "join public matches", "share court costs", "get paired with players at your level"; Padeon (11 ratings, EN+TR) — "Through the level-matching system, players can find suitable opponents, create matches, or join existing ones"; Raqet House (5 ratings) — "Açık maçlar oluşturun veya katılın; seviyenize uygun oyuncularla eşleşin" plus an "RQT puanı" city ranking. Other internationals are equally absent: MATCHi 5 TR ratings and no Turkish among 14 languages, Anybuddy 2 TR ratings (EN/FR/ES only), Sportya not in the TR store, Padel Manager 0 TR ratings.
findings.consequence: Splits the stated bet in two. The good half: no incumbent has claimed Istanbul, and Playtomic's own no-show handling is a manual Customer Care ticket that creates a debt and then explicitly voids the match ("The match result will be marked as void so it doesn't affect any player's level") — there is no persistent attendance number anywhere on a Playtomic profile, and none of Matchabit, Padeon or Raqet House advertises one. So Avenza's RELIABILITY-as-attendance really is unoccupied ground and the brief's bet holds. The bad half: the brief's claim that "nobody else knows... whether they are really the level they claim" is false in Istanbul as of now — three local racquet apps already assert match-derived level matching in Turkish. Avenza should stop pitching LEVEL as the differentiator and pitch attendance only, and should not expect padel alone to be defensible turf.

findings.claim: Playtomic charges players NOTHING for a plain court booking in every market checked, and its open-match fee is either hard-capped at about one euro (UK 20% capped at GBP 0.99; Poland 20% capped at PLN 3.99) or a low flat rate in emerging markets (Morocco 4%, no maximum) — so Avenza's uncapped flat 10% on every player share is roughly 2.5x the nearest comparable rate and applies where the incumbent charges zero.
findings.evidence: Playtomic's Service Fee help article renders its per-country fee schedule as PNG images; I downloaded three attachments by curl and read them. United Kingdom (attachment 39560464635793): Open Matches GBP 20.0%, Min 0.24, Max 0.99; Player Bookings NO FEE / NO FEE / NO FEE; Classes 4.0%; Courses 2.0%; Leagues 2.0%; Tournaments 4.0%. Poland (39560464619025): Open Matches PLN 20.0%, Min 1.24, Max 3.99; Player Bookings NO FEE, NO MIN, NO MAX. Morocco (39560464609681): Open Matches MAD 4.0%, Min 3, NO MAX; Player Bookings NO FEE, NO MIN, NO MAX. The article text adds that the fee "applies to every transaction processed online, except for wallet transactions", is not refunded on reservation or tournament cancellation, but IS refunded "if you delete yourself from an open match or if the match is canceled", and does not apply to vouchers, club wallets, or when the court fee is 0. Türkiye appears nowhere in the 36-country schedule.
findings.consequence: Prices Avenza's MONEY mechanic against a real ceiling. On Avenza's own worked example (720 TL court, 180 TL share), Avenza takes 18 TL; Playtomic's emerging-market rate (Morocco, 4%) would take 7.2 TL, and its UK/Poland structure would cap the take near one euro no matter how expensive the court. Two structural lessons Avenza's fee design currently ignores: (1) Playtomic charges 0% on a straight booking and monetises only the social open-match layer — Avenza taxing every player share, including a host booking a court to split with friends, is a strictly worse deal than the incumbent's free tier. (2) Playtomic caps the absolute fee; Istanbul padel courts run 1,000-3,000 TL/hour (unverified, from Turkish club-guide blogs), so an uncapped 10% on a 3,000 TL premium court means a 75 TL fee on a 750 TL share — a number no incumbent charges anywhere. Given host payouts are explicitly not built yet, the fee is also currently revenue Avenza cannot legally route; the cap-and-free-booking design is worth adopting before the payments provider conversation, not after.

findings.claim: Avenza's exact trust layer — a per-player attendance-reliability score used to filter out people who bail — is already shipping in Turkey inside HalıSaha+, which also ships level-based match placement, per-person cost split via a licensed PSP, and post-match player rating.
findings.evidence: Fetched the live Turkish App Store listing via the public iTunes API (https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=6761794919&country=tr), version 1.1.6, currentVersionReleaseDate 2026-08-31 (one day before this run). The description contains a dedicated section headed "GÜVEN PUANI — MAÇ İPTALİ DERDİ BİTSİN" (Trust Score — end the match-cancellation problem) with the bullets: "Halı Saha+ Güven Puanı, maçı satıp ekibi yarı yolda bırakanları filtreler" (the Trust Score filters out those who sell out a match and leave the team stranded) and "Her oyuncunun katılım güvenilirliği profilinde görünür" (every player's ATTENDANCE RELIABILITY is visible on their profile). Same listing: "Yapay zekâ seni performans puanına ve oyun sertliğine göre en dengeli maça yerleştirir" (AI places you in the most balanced match by performance score and play intensity); "herkes kendi payını öder" with "iyzico ile kredi kartı veya havale/EFT"; and "maç sonrası oyuncu değerlendirme, bekleme listesiyle kadro tamamlama". I then downloaded the 626px store screenshots and read them: screenshot 8 renders a live profile card with 177 Maç, 78/26/44 W-D-L, "4.0 Puan", "Puan Detayı (59 değerlendirme)" (rating detail from 59 evaluations) and "Seviye · Altın II · Lvl 14 · 7.541 XP", plus a location chip "İstanbul · Adalar +38" (39 neighbourhoods). Screenshot 7 shows district chat rooms live in Ümraniye, Pendik, Beyoğlu, Esenyurt (Istanbul, both shores). The vendor site halisahaplus.com corroborates the rating infrastructure — "Oyuncu sahayı, saha oyuncuyu, kaptan rakip takımı, katılımcı organizatörü puanlıyor" — and lists Istanbul among cities served, though it does not use the term "Güven Puanı", so the score's in-app rendering is verified only as far as the games-played + star-rating half of the profile card.
findings.consequence: This directly falsifies the brief's verbatim bet that "Nobody else knows whether the stranger you matched with will actually turn up." Someone in Turkey does, and says so in their store copy. Worse for sequencing: Avenza's RELIABILITY percentage, LEVEL number, post-game RATE step, neighbourhood onboarding step and per-person MONEY split are all present in one shipped Turkish app, and it has already crossed the bridge Avenza's brief explicitly defers — "host payouts are explicitly NOT built: that needs a payments provider and probably a licence" — by integrating iyzico. Avenza cannot lead with the trust layer as the differentiator in this market; it must either lead with something else or beat HalıSaha+ on execution of a claim the incumbent has already staked. Mitigating detail worth weighing: the listing has only 18 ratings (4.33) and its Discover screenshot still shows a seeded "HalıSaha+ Demo Park Halı Saha" venue in Ankara, so the claim is shipped but the marketplace is thin — the position is taken in copy, not yet won in liquidity.

findings.claim: Not one of the large Western pickup platforms ships a reliability SCORE; every one of them enforces attendance with money or with a binary ban instead — and the money version is the harder deterrent, already live in Turkey via Playtomic.
findings.evidence: Playtomic's public help centre (retrieved over plain HTTP with a browser user-agent after the fetch tool got 403; the page is public and unauthenticated) states verbatim: "Players can remove themselves up to 24 hours before the match starts. After this time, if they don't show up, it's considered a no-show... The absent player will be charged for the court fees. A debt is created in the app, and the no-show player must pay this debt in-app with a card in order to continue using the app." It adds "The match result will be marked as void so it doesn't affect any player's level" — i.e. Playtomic deliberately keeps no-shows OUT of its rating system and handles them financially. Plei's Terms state: "If a user does not show up for a confirmed Event and does not notify Plei before the Event start time, no refund or Event credit will be issued, and in addition, a $5 no-show fee will apply", plus "the user... may be banned from participating in other free Events. A user's account may be deactivated in the case of multiple no-shows." I read the full current App Store descriptions of the three largest Western pickup apps via the iTunes API — Plei (4.84, n=12,427), GoodRec (4.86, n=13,693), OpenSports (4.91, n=2,323) — and none mentions attendance, reliability, no-shows or a trust score; GoodRec's release notes offer only "Safety tools — Block and report players", and OpenSports offers "Check-in attendees" and "Group reviews" but no player reliability metric. The only two products positioning explicitly on a reliability score are tiny or unlaunched: LinkedUp ("Reliability Score based on real-world attendance, so you can see who follows through before you tap in"; "Lose score for no-shows"; "Extra score for showing up when the weather is unfavorable") has an email-capture waitlist and returned no App Store listing in a targeted iTunes search; Pickup LLC ("Built-in reputation system ensures reliable attendance") has 12 ratings. Playtomic is live in Turkey: TR App Store, 4.88, n=188, version 6.88.0 updated 2026-08-31.
findings.consequence: The cancellation-fee-vs-reliability-score distinction cuts against Avenza twice. First, it means the score is genuinely unbuilt at scale globally — that part of the bet survives — but it is unbuilt because the operators who have the most no-show data chose a different tool, and Playtomic explicitly voids no-show matches so they never touch its rating. That is evidence a score is the weaker instrument, not evidence of an unspotted gap. Second, Avenza's RELIABILITY percentage has no teeth: a 94% badge costs a defector nothing today, whereas Playtomic makes them pay the court fee before they can open the app again. Since Avenza already plans to touch money (the 10% fee on the player's share), the cheapest hardening of the trust layer is to attach a consequence to the existing MONEY mechanic — forfeit the player's share on a late bail — rather than to ship reputation alone. Note the interaction with ELIGIBILITY: because a game outside your level range is not shown at all, Avenza has no fallback surface on which a low-reliability user can still be offered games at a penalty, so reputation can only ever hide supply, never price it.

findings.claim: Charging the player a commission on their share of the court fee is not the norm in the Turkish market — every Turkish player-matching app examined takes zero cut of the split and monetises elsewhere or not at all.
findings.evidence: I read the store description of HalıSaha+'s payment flow and then read its store screenshot 4 directly: it renders a live 6-step "Rezervasyon Oluştur" wizard, "Adım 5 / 6: Ödeme Şekli", offering "Ben Ödüyorum" (Ödemeniz ₺3.500) versus the selected "Herkes Kendi Öder — Her oyuncu kendi payını öder. Toplam tutar kişi sayısına bölünür" (Ödemeniz ₺250). 3.500 ÷ 250 = exactly 14 players, so the split is at face value with no visible markup, under the banner "SAHA KİRALA / KENDİ PAYINI ÖDE — Online ödeme · nakit toplama derdi yok". Its site describes the product as "Ücretsiz kullan" with no commission stated. Corroborating across four more Turkish listings pulled from the TR App Store API: "Adam Eksik" states "Ödeme/komisyon yok — anlaşmalar ve ödemeler kullanıcılar arasında, elden" (no payment/commission; deals and payments are between users, in cash); Altıpas states "Altıpas ücretsizdir"; Smashmate (Turkish company, KAPLANS BİLGİ TEKNOLOJİLERİ) states "Finding opponents is free. Creating matches is free... No in-app purchases, no subscriptions" and routes booking to the club's own system; Sporsepeti (SPORSEPETİ TEKNOLOJİ A.Ş., 4.25, n=271, live since 2022) monetises with a Premium subscription — "You can send two match requests per week for free, or upgrade to Premium for unlimited requests" — not a transaction cut.
findings.consequence: Avenza's MONEY mechanic — 720 TL court, 180 TL share, 18 TL fee, 198 TL paid — asks the Kadıköy player to pay 10% more than the identical split costs them in HalıSaha+ or in cash, for a court Avenza does not own and a booking it does not hold. In a market where the free alternative already renders the split screen with a licensed PSP behind it, a player-side take rate is the single easiest thing for a competitor to point at. The two monetisation models actually validated in Turkish sports-social apps are subscription (Sporsepeti Premium, gating match requests) and the venue/organiser side (HalıSaha+ sells pitch automation, dynamic pricing and league tooling to işletmeler). Both are compatible with Avenza's existing surfaces — the BULLETIN already has "local sponsor slots" and VENUES pages are already derived from games — and neither requires the payments licence the brief flags as blocking. Recommend re-testing the 10% before it is built, because it is being built onto the one mechanic where a competitor charges zero.

findings.claim: The second half of Avenza's bet — that nobody knows whether a stranger "is really the level they claim" — is the more comprehensively owned half: level-verified matching has been shipping in Turkey since 2022, and Avenza's specific implementation (hide games outside your range) is a strictly weaker form of it than the ELO systems already in market.
findings.evidence: Sporsepeti (SPORSEPETİ TEKNOLOJİ A.Ş.) has been on the TR App Store since 2022-07-27, is at v2.16.0 with 271 ratings, and its current description reads: "Answer the level assessment questions... Add your score after each match and watch your ELO rating update... Before matching, check your opponent's profile to see their match history, win rate, rallies, badges, tournament results, and level. Every match helps you find opponents who are better suited to your level." Smashmate, a Turkish company shipping since 2026-08-05, states: "Every Smashmate player has an ELO rating. The player feed shows each opponent's ELO, win rate and match stats, so you get balanced, enjoyable games instead of one-sided ones" and its match-creation flow includes "Set the skill range" — Avenza's ELIGIBILITY mechanic, verbatim. HalıSaha+ screenshot 3, which I read directly, renders a shipped "Düello Arama İlanı" form with a four-tier selector Başlangıç / Orta / İleri / Profesyonel under the caption "Eşleştirmeler buna göre yapılır" (matches are made accordingly). Altıpas states "Her maç sonrası yapılan değerlendirmelerle gelişen bir oyuncu kartın oluşur" (a player card that evolves from post-match evaluations). Critically, all four derive level from RESULTS — ELO updated from recorded scores, win rate, match history — whereas Avenza's brief derives its 1.0–7.0 number from self-declaration nudged by peer ratings.
findings.consequence: For padel and tennis — two of Avenza's eight sports and the two with the most Istanbul commercial momentum — the level problem is solved by incumbents using outcome-derived ELO, and Avenza would be entering with a softer signal. This also exposes a cold-start defect in ELIGIBILITY: because a game whose level range excludes you is NOT SHOWN AT ALL and the host opt-in to "let others ask anyway" is off by default, a brand-new Avenza user whose 1.0–7.0 number is still just a self-declaration gets silently filtered out of supply before the RATE step has ever run — the loop cannot reach "Reputation" because "Discover" already hid the games. Sporsepeti's "level assessment questions" at signup and Smashmate's browse-before-signup ("browse padel matches and courts around you without signing up") are both direct answers to that problem that Avenza's deferred-signup onboarding currently lacks. The defensible move is to make the default a visible, askable "outside your range" state rather than invisibility, and to derive level from recorded results for the racket sports where the comparison to Sporsepeti will be made.

findings.claim: Avenza does NOT need its own TCMB payment licence to run the 10% split — but only in an architecture where it never owns the funds; Law 6493 Art. 12(2) makes the technical-facilitator exclusion conditional on the platform not being the owner of the transferred funds at any moment of the transaction, and the own-licence fallback now costs 40 million TL of minimum equity.
findings.evidence: Downloaded the TCMB's own guide 'Ödemeler Alanında Sunulan İş Modellerinin Ödeme Hizmeti Türleri ile İlişkilendirilmesine İlişkin Rehber' (Eylül 2022) and ran pdftotext on it. It reproduces the Art. 12(2) exclusion list verbatim, including: 'Teknik hizmet sağlayanların sunduğu... teknik hizmet sağlayanların işlemin herhangi bir anında transfer edilen fonun sahibi olmadığı hizmetler' and the commercial-agent limb 'Ödeme işleminin, gönderen ya da alıcı namına mal veya hizmet pazarlığına ya da alım satımına yetkili olan ticari temsilci aracılığıyla yapılması'. It then states flatly: 'Bankamız ve yukarıda sayılan ödeme hizmeti sağlayıcıları dışındaki kişilerin ödeme hizmeti sunması yasaktır.' Separately, pdftotext on the TCMB Tebliğ (Resmî Gazete 31 Ocak 2026, Sayı 33154) gives the new capital floors verbatim: '...asgari özkaynak yükümlülüğü tutarları, sırasıyla yirmi milyon Türk Lirası, kırk milyon Türk Lirası ve yüzbeş milyon Türk Lirası olarak belirlenmiştir. Bu Tebliğ 30/6/2026 tarihinde yürürlüğe girer.' — i.e. 20m TL for bill-payment-only institutions, 40m TL for a general ödeme kuruluşu, 105m TL for an e-money institution, up from 15m/30m/80m. The exemption is not free either: two law-firm sources put a 50 million TL rolling-12-month transaction threshold on the ticari temsilci exemption, above which an annual January notification to TCMB is due. iyzico's pazaryeri docs confirm the compliant route: money lands in iyzico's account first ('para ilk olarak iyzico hesabına gelir'), iyzico is merchant of record, and sub-merchants may be Bireysel, Şahıs Şirketi or Limited/A.Ş.
findings.consequence: The brief's line 'host payouts... needs a payments provider and probably a licence' is half right and half wrong, and the wrong half is the expensive one. There is no licence needed IF Avenza never touches the money — but that constraint has a hard product consequence for the MONEY mechanic and for CREATE. Any design where Avenza holds a balance, runs a wallet, escrows the pot until the game is played, refunds a no-show from Avenza's own float, or pays out to an individual host's IBAN, breaks the 'fonun sahibi olmadığı' condition and pushes Avenza toward a 40m TL capital requirement from 30 June 2026. The safe build: iyzico pazaryeri, each player charged individually at join time, and the VENUE as the alt üye işyeri — never the peer host. Making the host the sub-merchant is legally possible (iyzico supports 'Bireysel') but drags in gider pusulası and income-tax stopaj obligations on every payout to a private individual, which is a second, avoidable regulatory surface. This also means the ELIGIBILITY/level filter, not a payment hold, has to be what protects the game — and that the 'let others ask anyway' opt-in should not become a money-holding flow.

findings.claim: Avenza's 10% headline take is really about 3.5% net, because iyzico charges its ~4.29% + 0.25 TL commission on the FULL transaction amount and deducts it from the marketplace's share, not the seller's — so on the brief's own 198 TL example Avenza pays the PSP on all 198 TL while only 18 TL of it is Avenza's revenue.
findings.evidence: Scraped iyzico's own pricing and pazaryeri help pages with curl (WebFetch mangled them). Verbatim: 'iyzico komisyon ücreti, toplam işlem ücreti üzerinden hesaplanarak yeterli bakiyesi bulunan pazar yerinin payından kesilmektedir.' and 'iyzico üye iş yerlerine, her bir başarılı işlem için %4,29 ve 0,25 TL işlem ücreti uygulanmaktadır.' (non-company sellers: '%4,49'dan başlayan komisyon oranları + 0,25 TL'). KDV general rate is 20% since Karar 7346, Resmî Gazete 7 July 2023 no. 32241, effective 10 July 2023 (raised from 18%). Arithmetic on the brief's own numbers: player pays 198 TL; iyzico takes 4.29% x 198 + 0.25 = 8.74 TL out of Avenza's 18 TL; if the 18 TL is KDV-inclusive as Turkish consumer pricing normally is, net revenue is 18/1.20 = 15.00 TL; 15.00 - 8.74 = 6.26 TL retained = 3.5% of the player's 180 TL share, i.e. Avenza keeps ~35% of its own headline fee. On a real 2,800 TL indoor pitch split 14 ways the same maths yields ~6.98 TL per player, ~98 TL per game.
findings.consequence: The MONEY mechanic as specified is a ~3.5% business wearing a 10% label, and the gap is structural rather than a rate you can negotiate away: Avenza is paying card fees on the venue's money out of its own margin. Three levers, all of which change the UI copy: (a) raise the player fee to ~15-16% gross to net a true 10% — which would show as 180 TL + 28 TL on the join sheet and is well above the incumbent band in finding 3; (b) split the PSP cost with the venue via the pazaryeri commission agreement so the venue's share carries its own card cost; or (c) charge the venue a listing/commission rate instead of the player, which also removes the fee from the join flow entirely. Note the fee is also a KDV-bearing service supply, so ~1/6 of whatever is displayed is not revenue — the '10% fee, 18 TL' figure in the CREATE and join screens should be treated as gross-of-VAT, and per-sport unit economics should be modelled on ~3.5%, not 10%.

findings.claim: 10% is at the top of the market band, not below it: Playtomic charges exactly 10.0% on open matches in Greece and 20.0% in the US and Albania, but only 3.0-4.0% (Greece/Albania) or nothing at all (US) on plain court bookings — and it caps the fee in most markets, which Avenza does not.
findings.evidence: Playtomic's help centre 403s to WebFetch, so I pulled it with curl and found the per-country fee schedules are published as images. I downloaded three attachments and read them directly. Greece: Open Matches 10.0% EUR, min 0.3, NO MAX; Player Bookings 3.0%, min 0.3, NO MAX; Classes/Courses/Leagues/Tournaments 4.0%, min 0.3, max 2.9. United States: Open Matches 20.0% USD, min 0.29, max 0.99; Player Bookings / Classes / Courses / Leagues / Tournaments all 'NO FEE'. Albania: Open Matches 20.0%, min 34, max 120 ALL; everything else 4.0%, min 34, max 240-290 ALL. The article text states the fee 'applies to every transaction processed online, except for wallet transactions', is not refunded on a cancelled reservation, but IS refunded 'if you delete yourself from an open match or if the match is canceled'. Turkey does not appear anywhere in the 36-country fee list (Albania, Australia, Austria, Bahrain, Bosnia, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Indonesia, Ireland, Kenya, Kuwait, Latvia, Malta, Morocco, New Zealand, Oman, Poland, Pakistan, Qatar, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Slovenia, South Africa, Switzerland, Thailand, UK, UAE, US), although Playtomic is live on the Turkish App Store with 188 ratings.
findings.consequence: The incumbent price-discriminates on exactly the axis Avenza's core loop sits on: joining a stranger's open match is the expensive product (10-20%), booking a court you already have friends for is cheap or free (0-4%). That validates charging the fee on Discover->Join, but it means Avenza's flat, uncapped 10% is mispriced for the CREATE path where a host brings a known group — those users are being charged an open-match rate for a booking-rate product, and they are the users most likely to defect back to WhatsApp plus a phone call to the pitch. Greece is the closest comparable market and it prices open matches at exactly 10.0%, so the number is defensible; the missing piece is a cap. Playtomic's Payment Guidelines FAQ also shows how it de-risks a split without a reliability score: it puts a pre-authorisation hold on the booker for the whole court and only releases it two hours after the match once every player has paid, with the booker covering anyone who did not. That is a direct commercial substitute for Avenza's RELIABILITY percentage — the trust layer is being solved with a card hold rather than a reputation number, and a card hold works on day one with zero games played, which Avenza's score does not.

findings.claim: Avenza's hard-coded 720 TL court total is 3-4x below the real 2026 Istanbul price for a halı saha: the İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi 2026 tariff lists an outdoor floodlit halı saha at 2,250.00 TL/hour and an indoor one at 2,800.00 TL/hour, KDV included.
findings.evidence: WebFetch could not read the IBB tariff PDF, but it saved the binary, so I ran pdftotext -layout on it locally. Section 10, 'HALI SAHA KİRALAMA': 10.1 Açık Halı Saha Aydınlatmasız — Saat — 1.500,00; 10.2 Açık Halı Saha Aydınlatmalı — Saat — 2.250,00; 10.3 Kapalı Halı Saha — Saat — 2.800,00. Section 22: Tenis Kort Kiralama (Aydınlatmalı) — Saat — 500,00; (Aydınlatmasız) 300,00. Section 27: Açık basketbol sahaları Aydınlatmalı — Saat — 250,00. Note 18 of the tariff: 'Tarifede belirtilen ücretlere KDV dahil olup Tüzel şirketlere yapılacak kiralamalarda (A.Ş,Ltd.Şti.) fiyatlara KDV dahil değildir.' These are municipal prices, i.e. the floor; Turkish press reports private Istanbul pitches reaching 4,200 TL/hour, but that article (gzt.com) returned 403 and I could not corroborate it, so treat the private-sector figure as unverified.
findings.consequence: The MONEY worked example in the brief (720 TL -> 180 TL -> 18 TL fee) is a padel-shaped number applied to a football-shaped product, and it makes the fee look smaller than it will be. On the municipal indoor rate, 2,800 TL over 14 players is a 200 TL share and a 20 TL fee; on the unverified 4,200 TL private rate it is a 300 TL share and a 30 TL fee — a real number to put in the join sheet. More importantly, the tariff exposes an asymmetry that a flat 10% handles badly across Avenza's eight sports: a floodlit tennis court at 500 TL split two ways is a 250 TL share and a 25 TL fee, while a 2,250 TL halı saha split fourteen ways is a 160 TL share and a 16 TL fee. The tennis player pays more fee than the footballer for a cheaper court, purely because of party size. Either cap the fee in absolute TL (as Playtomic does in the US and Albania) or set the rate per sport. Separately, municipal facilities sell at a fixed published tariff with no third-party commission line, so IBB pitches are supply that VENUES pages can list but that the 10% cannot be levied on without the venue agreeing to be an alt üye işyeri.
