findings.claim: Every pickup-sports app that has reached mass scale in North America/Europe operates its own pre-booked, prepaid game slots and does NOT let ordinary users host games; the user-hosted model survives only at roughly one-sixth the scale.
findings.evidence: Pulled from the apps' own App Store listings via the public iTunes API on 2026-09-01 (itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=...&country=us) and from their own sites via curl. Plei's own description, verbatim: "We host soccer games across the US and ensure each game is well-organized with a combination of automation and a personal touch. Simply show up, play, and enjoy the game." Plei's feature list includes "Create groups with friends" but has NO create-a-game verb. GoodRec's own description: "1. Pick your sport and city 2. Choose your game 3. Show up and play" — again no create verb — plus "Live in 70+ cities across the US, Canada and Europe." goodrec.com/pickup-soccer/new-york-city (curled, tags stripped): "GoodRec organizes pickup soccer games every day in New York City" followed by a list of ~50 named facilities it plays at (Pier 40, Chelsea Waterside, Socceroof Sunset Park, Upper 90 …). volosports.com: "We handle the teams and gear", "13 Cities to play". US App Store rating counts as a scale proxy: GoodRec 13,693 (4.86), Plei 12,427 (4.84) — both own-inventory; OpenSports, the user-hosted/organiser platform, 2,323 (4.91). Volo's own listing names its 10 cities: Baltimore, Boston, Charleston, Denver, DC, New Jersey, New York, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle.
findings.consequence: Avenza's CREATE mechanic — any user hosts, picking sport/time/venue/format/level range/spots/cost split — is the supply model that no scaled Western operator uses as its primary supply. The winners buy the pitch hour and sell seats. For Avenza this says: treat Create as a retention feature for groups that already exist (the WhatsApp halı saha crew), and seed Kadıköy supply operationally by pre-booking off-peak slots at 3-5 Anatolian-shore venues and listing them as Avenza-run games. Without that, DISCOVER is an empty feed on launch day, and the ELIGIBILITY filter (which hides games outside your level range entirely) makes an empty feed look emptier.

findings.claim: The largest pickup app in North America treats mandatory prepayment — not an attendance or reliability score — as its stated answer to no-shows, and explicitly refuses to gate games by skill level.
findings.evidence: goodrec.com homepage FAQ, fetched by curl and tag-stripped, verbatim: "Do I have to pay for games in advance? Yes! We do this for a few reasons, but a major one is to ensure game quality. Nothing is worse than last-minute dropouts or no-shows. If everyone has a little skin in the game, then we limit both and can just enjoy the game!" Same FAQ, verbatim: "Do I need to be at a specific level to join a game? Unless clearly stated in the game title and description, our games are open to all levels!" The same page claims "1M Players | 100,000+ Games | 20,000+ 5* Reviews" — note GoodRec's own numbers are internally inconsistent, since its NYC page says "700,000+ Players | 100,000+ Games | 10,000+ Reviews", so treat the user counts as marketing, not measurement. Nowhere in GoodRec's site or App Store description is there any attendance percentage, reliability score or player rating.
findings.consequence: This directly contradicts Avenza's stated bet that "the trust layer is the differentiator. Nobody else knows whether the stranger you matched with will actually turn up." GoodRec does know — it took the money first. Avenza already collects at join (180 TL share + 18 TL fee), so the deposit IS the trust layer and it is already built; the RELIABILITY percentage is a nice profile ornament, not a moat, and should not be the thing the pitch rests on. Second hit: Avenza's ELIGIBILITY rule hides out-of-range games completely with "let others ask anyway" off by default. The operator with 100,000+ games run considers level-gating too costly to apply at all. In one district of one city, hiding inventory is the wrong default — ship the ask-anyway toggle ON, or show ineligible games greyed with a request button.

findings.claim: The best-documented pickup-sports 'find people to play with' failure did not die of an empty feed — it reached user scale and died of monetisation, and the founders' fix was to charge organisers, not players.
findings.evidence: 645 Ventures' published interview with Brian Litvack, co-founder of Sportsvite (2006, a consumer social network for recreational sports), fetched by curl. Verbatim: "Sportsvite got to reasonable scale in terms of users, but we found it difficult to market a consumer product and monetize the online community. We couldn't achieve a critical mass desired by advertisers. We started to realize that despite building out aspects of a successful online community it would be difficult to build a real consumer-based business in this market." And: "The organizers were the super-users in the Sportsvite community." They pivoted in 2009 to LeagueApps, B2B league software, which the same article says has since done "more than 7 million registrations" with "70+ employees". Corroborating pattern, two more: Sportaneous (2011 NYC pickup-games app, NYC BigApps winner) — Columbia Entrepreneurship's own startup page, opened: "In early 2013, Sportaneous was acquired by Greatist", after the product had already shifted to helping people "find and book sports activities and fitness classes". And Sportyfriends ApS (Denmark) now ships white-label venue apps from the same App Store publisher account (Padel Center Middelfart, id 6450256097, updated 2026-08-24; Padel iQ, id 6443525435) while its social app Sportyfriends (id 1391773424) has not shipped since 2025-10-30 and has 1 US rating. Meanwhile the surviving user-hosted platform prices for organisers: opensports.net/pricing, curled verbatim — "Event fees* 3%", "League & tournament fees* 3%", tiers at "$30 /mo", "$70 /mo", "$750+ /mo", and "* OpenSports transaction fees exclude Stripe fees".
findings.consequence: Avenza's MONEY mechanic takes 10% from the player's share and explicitly does not build host payouts ("that needs a payments provider and probably a licence"). That is 3.3x OpenSports' 3%, charged to the side of the market that the one documented survivor found was not the paying side — and with no payout, the Kadıköy captain who today collects 720 TL over WhatsApp gets nothing from Avenza while his players pay 18 TL more each. CREATE has no economic reason to exist for the host. Two live options: cut the player fee toward 3-5% and monetise the venue/organiser side instead, or accept that host payouts are not optional and price the host, not the player. The 10% number should be treated as an untested assumption, not a settled design.

findings.claim: Avenza's LEVEL mechanic — a numeric per-sport skill number on a 1.0-7.0 scale, nudged by post-game results, used to gate a match's level range — is already shipped by Playtomic on effectively the same scale, and Playtomic is live on the Turkish App Store with 188 ratings at 4.88 while carrying no Turkish localisation.
findings.evidence: playerhelp.playtomic.com level article, fetched by curl with a browser UA (WebFetch was 403'd), verbatim: "you'll complete a brief level assessment... From there, your level will adjust automatically based on your match results", with the factors listed as "Match result – Opponent levels – Partner level – Your reliability score". Note Playtomic's "reliability" is confidence in the level estimate, NOT attendance: "When you're new to Playtomic, your reliability is low, so your level will fluctuate more dramatically as the system learns your true skill level." Playtomic's own blog gives the level chart as Beginner 1-2 / Lower intermediate 3-4 / Intermediate 5-6 / Advanced 7-8. Playtomic's Turkish App Store listing (itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=1242321076&country=tr, fetched 2026-09-01): 188 ratings, 4.88 average, version 6.88.0 released 2026-08-31, first released 2017-11-02; languageCodesISO2A is ['CA','DA','NL','EN','FI','FR','DE','IT','NB','PL','PT','ES','SV'] — TR is absent. Its description already contains Avenza's create-and-split loop verbatim: "Create private matches at your favorite padel club... Make them public so that other players can join in the fun", "over 16,000 courts worldwide", "you will have the option to pay the court fees in full yourself or split them with the other players." Separately, a Turkish company shipped an ELO version of the same idea three weeks ago: SmashMate (id 6760764730, KAPLANS BILGI TEKNOLOJILERI TICARET LTD, first release 2026-08-05, 17 TR ratings), "Every Smashmate player has an ELO rating... Set the skill range", and it deliberately avoids the payments problem: "Booking and payment happen through the club's own system; Smashmate points you to the right court."
findings.consequence: For padel specifically, Avenza's LEVEL is not a differentiator — it is Playtomic's system with the stars redrawn, and a local Istanbul startup shipped an ELO variant last month. Two consequences. (1) Stop pitching the 1.0-7.0 level as novel; the defensible ground is multi-sport plus neighbourhood (halı saha + basketball + running in Kadıköy), which neither Playtomic nor SmashMate touches. (2) The two real openings are exactly the gaps: Playtomic has no Turkish localisation at all, and SmashMate explicitly refuses to handle money. Avenza's bilingual TR/EN onboarding and its in-app cost split are the only mechanics in the brief that neither incumbent offers in Istanbul — so those, not the trust layer, are what the product should lead with. Caveat: I could not verify Playtomic has bookable Istanbul clubs, so the 188 TR ratings may partly be Turkish users playing abroad.

findings.claim: Credit-plus-outlink does not clear Avenza to AI-summarise Hürriyet or NTV Spor articles: Hürriyet's terms bar attributed quotation outright and ban automated collection, NTV requires prior written permission, and FSEK m.36/II's press-summary exception is confined to social/political/economic daily articles appearing in a newspaper or magazine — which excludes sport and excludes broadcaster NTV Spor entirely.
findings.evidence: FSEK m.36/II text (via LEXPERA consolidated text + search corroboration): "Gazete veya dergilerde çıkan içtimai, siyasi veya iktisadi günlük meselelere müteallik makale ve fıkraların iktibas hakkı sarahaten mahfuz tutulmamışsa aynen veya işlenmiş şekilde diğer gazete ve dergiler tarafından alınması ... serbesttir. İktibas hakkı mahfuz tutulsa bile sözü geçen makale ve fıkraların kısaltılarak basın özetleri şeklinde alınması ... caizdir." I downloaded the peer-reviewed analysis (Soykan, "Fikrî Mülkiyet Hukukunda Basın İktibasları", İÜHFM C.LXVII S.1-2 s.183-208, 2009) as PDF from DergiPark and ran pdftotext. p.197: "FSEK m. 36/I'den farklı olarak tüm basın organlarında yer alan yayınlar, bu fıkranın uygulanma alanında değildir. Dolayısıyla radyodan veya televizyondan yapılacak alıntılar FSEK m. 36/II'nin kapsamına girmez" — so TV/radio-origin content (NTV Spor) is outside m.36/II and falls under m.80/(C) broadcaster rights requiring written permission. p.198: "günlük olaylara ilişkin olmayan gazete ve dergi içeriğinin iktibası hususunda FSEK m. 36/II uygulanmaz" — the provision enumerates only içtimai/siyasi/iktisadi subject matter; sport is not among them. FAVOURABLE point for Avenza, same page: "İktibas serbestisinden yararlanacak olan yayın organı konusunda ise kanun bir sınırlama koymamıştır" — the law does NOT restrict who may take, so being an app rather than a newspaper is not itself fatal. Limit on the summary, p.199-200: "yapılacak özet ... yazının aslına olan ihtiyacı ortadan kaldıramaz. Yalnızca yazının içeriği hakkında sınırlı bir bilgi vererek kamuoyunu yazının aslını okumaya yönlendirecek şekilde olabilir" and a summary that removes the need for the original "haksız rekabet oluşturur" (constitutes unfair competition). Attribution standard, FSEK m.36/son quoted at p.201: "iktibas edilen gazete, dergi ve ajansın ... adı, tarih ve sayısından başka makale sahiplerinin adı, müstear adı veya alameti zikredilmek icap eder" — publisher name alone is NOT compliant; date, issue and the author's name are required. Hürriyet kullanım koşulları, fetched: "izin alınmadan, kaynak gösterilerek dahi iktibas edilemez" (cannot be excerpted even with attribution, without permission) and "robot, örümcek veya başka otomatik aletler ya da manuel süreçler kullanmayacaklarını". NTV kullanım koşulları: all news and materials usable "only with written permission from the Company".
findings.consequence: Hits BULLETIN directly. The spec's "credited to the publisher and out-linked, never reproduced" is not a defence in Turkey, and two of the three named publishers (Hürriyet, NTV Spor) are the worst possible choices — one expressly reserves iktibas and bans crawlers, the other is a broadcaster outside the newspaper exception. Three concrete changes: (1) the credit string must carry author name + date + issue/URL, not just "Milliyet"; (2) for sport, fall back to FSEK m.36/I ("günlük havadisler ve haberler serbestçe iktibas olunabilir") and re-spec world-sport Bulletin items as fact-cards — score, transfer, result, who/when — generated from the event rather than as AI summaries of a named article, because m.36/I protects the fact and not the article's expression; (3) source via publisher RSS/API or a licensed wire (Anadolu Ajansı), never a crawler, since Hürriyet's robot ban is a contract/unfair-competition hook that survives regardless of how the copyright question comes out.

findings.claim: A bill before the TBMM since 10 February 2026 names Avenza's exact Bulletin mechanic — "otomatik özet" and "haber kartı/paneli" — as a paid act and expressly denies safe harbour to link-sharing that carries any snippet; Avenza escapes only because it sits below a 100,000,000 TL revenue / 1,000,000 monthly-active-user threshold.
findings.evidence: I downloaded the bill text itself from the TBMM CDN (623 KB PDF, HTTP 200) and extracted it with pdftotext. MADDE 3(6): "Ek Unsur: Salt bağlantı (URL) paylaşımı dışında; haber başlığı, spot, özet/snippet, otomatik özet, küçük görsel/thumbnail, video veya ses önizlemesi, haber kartı/paneli, trend/kategori kutusu, içerik üzerinde önbellekleme veya benzeri sunum unsurlarını". MADDE 2 carve-out: "Salt bağlantı (URL) paylaşımı ile kullanıcıların kişisel ve ticari olmayan paylaşımları; Ek Unsur içermemesi ve Ekonomik Değer Yaratan Kullanım niteliği taşımaması hâlinde bu Kanun kapsamında değerlendirilmez" — i.e. the only safe form is a bare URL with no snippet at all. MADDE 3(5) defines Ekonomik Değer Yaratan Kullanım to include revenue from "reklam, abonelik, komisyon/işlem ücreti, sponsorluk" AND non-revenue benefit "kullanıcı edinimi, elde tutma, etkileşim artışı veya hizmetin değerlenmesine katkı" — Avenza's Bulletin has local sponsor slots and Avenza takes a 10% commission, and the feed's stated job is retention. MADDE 3(8) threshold: "Türkiye kaynaklı yıllık brüt dijital hizmet geliri 100.000.000 Türk Lirasını aşan veya Türkiye'de aylık ortalama aktif kullanıcı sayısı 1.000.000'un üzerinde olan dijital platformu; aynı ekonomik bütünlük içindeki platformların eşiklerinin birlikte değerlendirilmesi suretiyle belirlenen platformu". Corroborated independently by two Turkish law firms: Paksoy (Apr 2026) confirms the 10 Feb 2026 filing, BTK as regulator, a 1% floor of Turkey revenue on annual payments (BTK may set 1-3%), fines of 1-5% of Turkey revenue rising to 10% for repeat violations, and status "under examination in relevant TBMM commissions"; Tevetoğlu Legal (17 Feb 2026) and Pekin (19 Feb 2026) also cover it.
findings.consequence: Hits BULLETIN and, via the definition of economic value, MONEY. This is not a launch blocker — a Kadıköy pilot is orders of magnitude below 1M Turkish MAU — but it fixes the ceiling: the Bulletin cannot be a load-bearing growth engine, because success at scale converts it into a licensing liability with a 1%-of-Turkey-revenue floor. Build the Discover header so the world-sport strand is a swappable source behind one interface, with two fallbacks already wired: Avenza's own local items only (new venues, court prices, leagues with spots), or a licensed wire. Also note the aggregation rule "aynı ekonomik bütünlük içindeki platformların eşiklerinin birlikte değerlendirilmesi" — an acquisition by a larger Turkish platform pools the thresholds, so this is a diligence item, not just a scale item. Caveat: this is a bill in commission, not enacted law.

findings.claim: No sports booking or match-finding utility app in the Turkish App Store runs an editorial news feed — across 139 unique apps returned by eight Turkish-language queries, every news-carrying app was a pure scores/news product or a league's own app.
findings.evidence: I queried the public iTunes Search API at country=tr for eight terms (padel, tenis, spor sosyal, maç bul, saha rezervasyon, basketbol maç, kort rezervasyon, spor arkadaş), deduped to 139 unique trackIds, and regex-scanned every description for haber|bülten|news|gündem|editorial|dergi|magazine|blog. 11 apps matched. Of those: Flashscore, Mackolik (42,171 TR ratings), NBA, Soloscore and Premier Padel are scores/news/league products; three "Sosyal Medya'da <kulüp>" apps are fan-news readers; and the two halı saha matches are false positives — Altıpas's "çevrendeki uygun oyunculara anında haber gitsin" means a push notification, Yenigün Tenis's "Önceden haber alın" means be informed. Zero booking or match-finding apps carry editorial content. Cross-checked outside Turkey via the same API: Playtomic v6.88.0 (188 TR ratings) never mentions news anywhere in its description; Spond (8,142 GB ratings) returns no news lines; Strava's only "feed" is the activity feed — "your feed on Strava is filled with real efforts from real people"; Sofascore's US listing (76,660 ratings) returns no news lines in its description. Onefootball is editorial-first ("Stay updated on all MLS soccer scores, matches and news"), i.e. a news product, not a utility with news bolted on. The one Turkish attempt at the hybrid runs the other way round: Soloscore (Soloscore Teknoloji A.Ş., released 13 Jun 2026, still v0.2.1, 74 ratings) is news-and-social-first — "Live scores, match details, fixtures, and the latest football news" plus "Social interaction with football fans" — with no booking or match-organising layer at all.
findings.consequence: Hits BULLETIN. The pattern is genuinely unowned in this category, but that is a warning as much as an opening: Turkish sports-news attention is already consolidated in apps the target user has installed — Mackolik at 42,171 TR ratings and Sofascore at 19,119 — so a world-sport strand inside a Kadıköy match-finder competes on their turf with none of their data, while carrying the entire legal exposure of Findings 1 and 2. The half that is defensible is the local half, because it is generated by VENUES (pages derived from games played there) and CREATE (hosted games with spots), which no rival can copy without the same supply. Recommended split: keep local items as the Discover header, demote world sport to a small out-linked strip of bare fact-cards or drop it, and measure whether the header's taps come from local or world items before investing further.

findings.claim: Three of the four onboarding numbers in Avenza's brief do not survive tracing to source, and the category leader has moved in the opposite direction — Playtomic now requires a verified phone number from every new account.
findings.evidence: (1) "77% leave within three days": I fetched Andrew Chen's post. Verbatim: "the average app loses 77% of its DAUs within the first 3 days after the install." Source is Quettra, panel of "over 125 million" ANDROID devices, five months starting 1 January 2015 — Android-only, eleven years old, and about DAUs not departures; the post itself caveats that losing DAUs "doesn't mean complete inactivity." (2) "Activation averages 37.5%": traces to Userpilot's 2024 SaaS Product Metrics Benchmark Report. Userpilot sells product-adoption software, so this is a vendor benchmark, and secondary summaries contradict each other on the sample — "547 SaaS companies" in some, "first-party activation data from 62 SaaS companies" in others. The report page returned HTTP 404 when I fetched it, so I could not confirm n at source. Either way it is B2B SaaS, not consumer mobile in Turkey. (3) "Social sign-on converts 2-3x": I could find no source for 2-3x. The best recoverable figure is 20-40% (attributed to a Gigya marketing manager, repeated by LoginRadius and Bread & Butter) — that is 1.2-1.4x, not 2-3x. Corbado's 2026 benchmark page explicitly refuses to supply a number: "Social login conversion rate is not a single number you can copy from a case study." (4) "Deferred signup lifts activation 10-30%": traces only to vendor blogs (VMobify, Rownd) citing unlinked "Localytics" research; the Rownd URL served an unrelated page when I fetched it, so the underlying study is unverified. MEANWHILE, on competitor behaviour: Playtomic's App Store release notes for v6.88.0 (fetched from country=tr, released 31 Aug 2026) say verbatim "New users will go through a quick phone verification to keep our community safe" and "We've enhanced phone verification for social features"; Playtomic's Help Centre article "How to create your account in Playtomic" (updated 9 June 2026) states a mobile phone number is required to complete account setup on top of Apple/Google/Facebook/email sign-up, plus an email verification link. GoodRec goes the other way on discovery only: goodrec.com/pickup-soccer/philadelphia is fully public with no login, listing venue and date/time ("Friends Select Saturday, February 28, 2026 at 09:00 AM Duration: 60"), and gates only the join behind "JOIN VIA APP".
findings.consequence: Hits ONBOARDING and, more importantly, RELIABILITY. Deferred signup itself is still right — GoodRec proves the discovery half works with zero account — but stop citing the four numbers, because a reviewer who traces them finds one Android panel from 2015, one B2B SaaS vendor survey with a disputed n, and two figures with no primary source, and will discount the rest of the brief with them. The load-bearing point is the second one: the RELIABILITY percentage is only worth what it costs to abandon it. With Google/Apple only and no password or phone anywhere, a host who no-shows and burns a 62% score re-enters at a fresh 100% with a second Google account in under a minute, and ELIGIBILITY compounds this because a re-registered user also re-declares their LEVEL free of any rating history. Playtomic added phone verification at exactly the scale where that started to bite. Avenza does not need it at signup — put it at the first JOIN of a paid game, which is where the 10% fee already needs a payment instrument, so the friction lands on a step the user has already decided to take.

competitors.name: HalıSaha+ (Rezervasyon, Kadro) — formerly SahaGol
competitors.whatItDoes: BOTH books and matches. Full football ecosystem: pitch booking with iyzico online payment, "Hızlı Maç Bul" AI matchmaking on district + time + level, a Güven Puanı (trust/attendance score) that filters no-shows, rentable goalkeepers and kit, team/opponent "Düello" matching, tournaments and league automation with live scores, a "Tribün" social feed, and a venue-operator SaaS panel with dynamic pricing. Live: v1.1.6 shipped 2026-08-31; iOS-only, no Android package found. Rating 4.33 from only 18 ratings.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: The most dangerous overlap in the market. Directly duplicates RELIABILITY (Güven Puanı: "Her oyuncunun katılım güvenilirliği profilinde görünür"), LEVEL-based matching, post-match rating that feeds the profile, MONEY (per-person cost split — "herkes kendi payını öder" — but with real iyzico rails, the payments provider Avenza explicitly deferred), and VENUES. Does not overlap Avenza's multi-sport scope or BULLETIN.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Yes, and specifically Kadıköy. halisahaplus.com names Kadıköy, Beşiktaş, Çankaya, Nilüfer, Karşıyaka, Selçuklu as districts, and Istanbul, Ankara, İzmir, Bursa, Antalya and 9 more cities. Turkish company: Parpali Yazilim ve Bilisim Hizmetleri Ticaret Ltd Sti. One 5-star review references live use at a tournament in Ürgüp.

competitors.name: Altıpas Halı Saha Maçı Bul
competitors.whatItDoes: MATCHES, does not book. Free social football platform: create a match in minutes, post a one-off "eksik oyuncu" ad by position and district, find opponent teams by level and area, community/neighbourhood group chat with polls, A/B team balancing and a formation editor, tournaments and club tryouts, and a player card that grows from post-match ratings (matches, wins, goals, assists, MVP votes, community ranking). Ships WhatsApp roster paste and install-free link joining. Bilingual TR/EN, Google/Apple/email sign-in. Live and shipping: v2.1.0 on 2026-08-27, Play updated 26 Ağu 2026. 4.08 from 26 ratings; 10,000+ Play installs.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Closest to Avenza's CREATE and Discover->Join loop, and to the ad concept. Player card overlaps the rating/games-played half of RELIABILITY but has no attendance or no-show percentage. Uses level only for opponent-team matching, never to hide games from a player. Also matches Avenza's bilingual TR/EN and Google/Apple onboarding choices exactly.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Istanbul-first by design. altipas.app states "İlk pilot maçların İstanbul'da sınırlı sayıda anlaşmalı sahada başlatılması planlanmaktadır." Districts are a first-class filter throughout the product. Turkish developer (Emre Kaan Akcay).

competitors.name: Santra: Halı Saha & Kadro
competitors.whatItDoes: MATCHES and organises; no booking or payment. Explicitly positioned against the WhatsApp group. Internal (split your own team) or external (find an opponent) matches, automatic squad balancing from player stats, score entry confirmed by the opposing team, and a 6-attribute FIFA-style rating card (pace/shot/pass/dribble/defence/physical, plus keeper-specific attributes) with a Bronze→Silver→Gold→Diamond tier and a separate fair-play score. Live: v1.8.0 on 2026-08-24. 5.0 from 13 ratings, but only 50+ Play installs.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Its opening sentence is Avenza's ad concept. Its skill card is the direct alternative design to Avenza's LEVEL — visible, multi-dimensional, gamified, and peer-assigned rather than a hidden matching number. Its "fair play puanı" is the nearest thing in the market to a behavioural score other than HalıSaha+'s Güven Puanı.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Turkish app and developer (Furkan Dede), santra-app.com. No district-level targeting found; nothing Kadıköy-specific.

competitors.name: Adam Eksik
competitors.whatItDoes: MATCHES, but as classifieds. The oldest and one of the largest: a player-finding site plus forum ("Halı saha oyuncularının sosyal medyası ve halı saha oyuncu bulma sitesi"), Play listing since 2 Ara 2019, 10,000+ installs, 3.94 from 121 ratings — but last updated 12 Eki 2024, so semi-dormant. Critically, it does not own the transaction: the Play listing tells users to invite players via the phone number on their profile.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Occupies Avenza's Discover->Join intent with none of the loop closed: no LEVEL, no RELIABILITY, no ratings, no MONEY. It is the digitised manual status quo. Its 10k installs versus the 2026 cohort's ~50–1000 shows demand exists at a scale nobody new has captured.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Yes, active Istanbul use. A Play review reads: "İstanbul'da son 1 yılda 50 farklı maça katılma şansı yakaladım bu uygulama sayesinde" (found 50 different matches in Istanbul in the last year through this app). Forum threads are city-organised (Adana, Kocaeli/Körfez).

competitors.name: Halısahavar
competitors.whatItDoes: DEAD but still the category's rating leader. Matching-side product: find a partner, find a match, post for a missing position ("ADAM MI EKSİK?"), find an opponent team, build a squad with formations, and create an "HSV kartı" player card with self-selected position and attributes. 4.60 from 154 ratings — more than all 17 apps launched in 2025–26 combined.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Historic proof that the missing-player and opponent-finding problems pull real Turkish demand, and a cautionary tale: it had the audience and abandoned the product. No RELIABILITY, no level-gated ELIGIBILITY, no MONEY.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Turkish, halisahavar.com still resolves (HTTP 200) with SEO blog content, but the product is abandoned: iOS v1.2.4 last updated 2022-06-29, Android last updated 29 Ara 2021 — over 4.5 years without a release.

competitors.name: Maçla - Halı Saha Maçı Bul
competitors.whatItDoes: MATCHES only. Browse nearby match ads and join instantly, position-based search for missing players (keeper/defender/forward), a profile stating your position and playing style, and in-app messaging. Shipping fast: v2.0.3 on 2026-08-29 added iOS home-screen widgets for match-post expiry and a 60 FPS chat rewrite. 3.94 from 17 ratings.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Overlaps Discover->Join and the messaging Avenza has not built. Notably has NO level and NO reliability mechanic — matching is by position and area only. One 1-star review ("yetersiz — geliştirilmeli", insufficient, needs development) and a 4-star asking for video in listings are the only critical signals in the TR review feed.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Turkish developer (Taha Goktug Lengerli), Turkish-only listing. A review notes it needs awareness across all "81 İl" (81 provinces), implying no single-city concentration yet.

competitors.name: Saha Bul / BiHalısaha / Pasona / SporPin / Hadimaça / Olleyy
competitors.whatItDoes: BOOKING-side cluster, the other half of the map. These sell pitch discovery, live availability calendars, online payment/deposit and a venue-operator management panel; player matching is absent or vestigial. Hadimaça extends beyond football into basketball, volleyball, tennis, yoga, pilates and dance studios and adds referee booking. Saha Bul 4.54 from 26 ratings (upd 2026-06-16); BiHalısaha 4.60 from 15 (2026-04-15); Pasona 5.0 from 11 (2026-08-29); Hadimaça 5.0 from 3 (2026-07-09); Olleyy 1.0 from 1.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Overlaps VENUES only, and inverts Avenza's approach — they hold the supply relationship and the booking, whereas Avenza derives venue pages from games played there. None has LEVEL, RELIABILITY, or player-to-player matching. Hadimaça is the only competitor whose sport list approaches Avenza's eight-sport breadth, and it does so on the booking side.
competitors.turkeyPresence: All Turkish. Hadimaça (DEDE GROUP TEKNOLOJI LTD) and Pasona are nationwide-facing; SporPin exposes an Istanbul district-filtered venue search at sporpin.com/SahaBul/?sid=34. No Kadıköy-specific positioning found in any of them.

competitors.name: The "eksik oyuncu" name cluster (SahaGO, Halısaha Kadrom, Halı Saha Kadro, Adam Eksik Mi, Dördüncü Eksik, Eksik Adam, Benimsaham, MaçYap, Online Halısaham)
competitors.whatItDoes: A long tail of near-identical 2025–26 launches. Roughly split between squad/lineup utilities with no network (Halısaha Kadrom, Halı Saha Kadro, Kickoro, Lineup Coach — these are offline team-splitters, not marketplaces) and thin matching apps (SahaGO adds QR-based points and leaderboards; MaçYap covers football/volleyball/basketball but last shipped 2025-03-13; Online Halısaham has player rating and messaging but last shipped 2025-01-07). A separate iTunes TR search for "eksik oyuncu" returns seven apps with functionally interchangeable names, five updated within the last three months.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Individually negligible; collectively they are the evidence that Avenza's football wedge is the single most contested surface in Turkish sports apps and the one where its differentiator is weakest. They validate the pivot argument: Avenza's defensible ground is the multi-sport LEVEL (padel, tennis, basketball, volleyball) where no equivalent cluster exists.
competitors.turkeyPresence: All Turkish, all national in framing. MaçYap (macyap.com.tr) and Online Halısaham are functionally abandoned (last updates Mar 2025 and Jan 2025). None targets Kadıköy or the Anatolian shore.

competitors.name: Playtomic
competitors.whatItDoes: Category leader for racquet booking and social matchmaking. Padel, tennis, pickleball only. 6,879 clubs in its own sitemap, claims 16,000+ courts and 1M+ players in its App Store copy. Court booking, open (public) matches with level ranges, cost splitting, leagues/tournaments, chat, per-sport 0-7 level with a reliability % confidence score, Premium subscription that removes booking/match/cancellation fees.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Near-total on LEVEL (0-7 per sport, questionnaire-seeded, match-derived, peer-review nudged), on CREATE (any user hosts a public match), on the cost-split money flow, and on VENUES (club pages). Opposite on ELIGIBILITY (shows out-of-range matches with a request-a-spot path rather than hiding them). Uses Avenza's word "reliability" for a different concept. Does NOT have Avenza's attendance percentage — no-shows are a manual Customer Care ticket producing a debt, and the match is voided rather than scored against the player.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Effectively none. 188 TR App Store ratings vs 75,597 ES / 39,943 IT / 33,040 GB. No Turkish among its 13 app languages. No /tr/ locale in its sitemap (es/it/pt/fi/sv/nl/fr/de only). No Istanbul or Turkish city landing page among 52 padel/tennis city pages that do include Doha, Dubai, Singapore, Cape Town and Nicosia. 0 of 140 randomly sampled club pages were in Turkey. Türkiye absent from its 36-country service-fee schedule, implying no TRY payment processing.

competitors.name: Matchabit - Padel, Tennis
competitors.whatItDoes: Turkey-adjacent racquet booking and matchmaking app (seller birfincankafein OU). Real-time club/court discovery and booking, private and public matches, court cost sharing, and per its own listing "an advanced leveling system that adjusts based on match outcomes", plus win/loss and match-history stats. Tennis, padel, pickleball.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Hits LEVEL (match-outcome-adjusted), CREATE (public matches), and the cost-split MONEY flow simultaneously — the closest single overlap with Avenza's racquet-side loop. English only, no Turkish localisation. No attendance or reliability mechanic advertised.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Live in the TR App Store with 36 ratings, v1.2.2 released 2026-08-10. Surfaced as a top result for the Turkish query "padel rezervasyon".

competitors.name: Padeon
competitors.whatItDoes: Turkish racquet-sports platform (PADEON TEKNOLOJI VE YAZILIM, a Turkish A.S.). Player discovery with a "level-matching system", match creation and joining, court reservation and payment across "contracted facilities across Türkiye", tournaments, performance/match history, plus a club-side management panel with revenue and occupancy reporting.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Overlaps LEVEL (level-matching), CREATE (match creation/joining), VENUES (facility pages) and the payment step. Crucially it is bilingual EN+TR — the same bilingual posture Avenza claims. Racquet-only, so no overlap on football/basketball/volleyball. No attendance/reliability mechanic advertised.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Turkish company, Turkish-language app, claims contracted facilities nationwide. 11 TR ratings, v1.1.1 released 2026-08-19 — early but explicitly national in scope.

competitors.name: Raqet House
competitors.whatItDoes: Turkish padel platform (NEXORA LABS, Turkish LLC). Turkish-language listing: discover nearby padel clubs with court and price info, book courts, "create or join open matches; match with players at your level", in-app messaging and match chats, an "RQT puanı" rating that ranks you in your city, favourite clubs with campaign notifications, plus a club admin panel.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Overlaps LEVEL (seviye matching plus an RQT city ranking), CREATE (açık maç), VENUES (club pages with prices), and messaging. The RQT city leaderboard is a reputation surface Avenza does not have. Padel only. No attendance percentage advertised.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Turkish-built, Turkish-language, positions itself as "Türkiye'nin padel platformu". 5 ratings, v1.4.5 released 2026-09-01 — actively shipping.

competitors.name: PFM - Play for More
competitors.whatItDoes: Turkish digital sports platform (PFM SPOR TEKNOLOJILERI A.S.) letting players of all levels challenge each other, organise matches and training, and book at partner clubs or courts in-app. Runs subscriptions. Its web arm playformore.app is the booking system for Istanbul's Ista Padel.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Overlaps CREATE and the matchmaking/booking loop, and is already the incumbent booking rail at at least one Istanbul padel/tennis club. Listing mentions "players of all levels" but does not describe a numeric level scale; no attendance mechanic advertised.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Strong and specifically Istanbul. Turkish company, 84 TR ratings (3.80 avg — the weakest rating of the Turkish racquet cohort), v2.6.10 released 2026-07-04. Named in Istanbul padel guides as the reservation system used by Ista Padel.

competitors.name: Kort: Find Tennis Partners
competitors.whatItDoes: Tennis partner-finding app from Turkish developer Distant Teknoloji. Profile with experience level and location, algorithmic partner matching, fast messaging, open invitations others can join at a set place and time, a "Kort Challenge" for recording match results, tournaments, and progress tracking. Premium adds coach/partner profiles and unlimited discovery.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: This is Avenza's Discover -> Join -> Play -> Rate loop for tennis, minus courts and money. Open invitations are Avenza's CREATE; experience level is a self-declared LEVEL. It monetises by subscription rather than a transaction fee, which is a direct alternative to Avenza's 10% cut. No attendance/reliability score.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Highest-rated Turkish racquet social app found: 549 TR ratings at 4.83, the largest TR rating count in the racquet cohort including Playtomic. v3.7.6, though last released 2026-01-15 — the only one in the cohort not shipping recently.

competitors.name: SiberTenis
competitors.whatItDoes: Club-management-first platform "used by Turkey's largest tennis and racket sports clubs": online court reservations, tournaments and DEFI leagues, online payments, membership management, group and private lessons, a coach module with attendance/earnings tracking, a parent portal, and AI-generated parent bulletins. Also lets you "find partners to play tennis or other racket sports".
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Owns the supply side Avenza does not have — the clubs themselves. Overlaps VENUES and partner-finding, and its digital attendance tracking is the nearest thing in the Turkish market to Avenza's RELIABILITY, though it is coach-facing lesson attendance, not peer no-show reputation. No player-facing level scale advertised.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Turkish company (TOKEN YAZILIM A.S.), 233 TR ratings, v2.1.2 (2025-10-28). Claims deployment at Turkey's largest racquet clubs — the strongest club-side foothold found.

competitors.name: MATCHi
competitors.whatItDoes: Nordic racquet-sport court booking network (MATCHi AB) covering tennis, padel, badminton and squash, with club booking systems and player matchmaking.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Booking and matchmaking overlap in principle, but it is not a competitor for Avenza's trust layer and is racquet-only.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Negligible. 5 TR App Store ratings. 14 app languages, none of them Turkish.

competitors.name: Anybuddy
competitors.whatItDoes: Padel and tennis court booking app (French origin), aggregating club availability for instant booking.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Booking only; no meaningful overlap with LEVEL, RELIABILITY or CREATE.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Negligible. 2 TR App Store ratings; app languages EN/FR/ES only. anybuddyapp.com/en/istanbul and /turkey both returned 301 redirects rather than city pages.

competitors.name: Sportya
competitors.whatItDoes: Amateur tennis competition and ranking platform, Romanian origin, organising tournament circuits with player rankings.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Ranking/level overlap in principle, but competition-circuit shaped rather than pick-up-game shaped.
competitors.turkeyPresence: None found. Does not appear in the Turkish App Store at all (a TR store search for "sportya" returned only unrelated apps such as WhatsApp and Flashscore). sportya.net/en returned a 301 I did not follow cross-host, so its level system is unverified.

competitors.name: Padel Mates
competitors.whatItDoes: Swedish multi-racquet app (padel, pickleball, tennis, badminton, squash) with in-app booking and payment, facility map, community groups, game finder, "smart match suggestions... based on your skill level", cost splitting with friends, chat, and "performance feedback". PRO subscription at $6/month, $29/6mo, $49/year.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Closest feature-for-feature clone of Avenza's racquet-side loop including skill-level suggestions, cost splitting and post-game performance feedback — but sells a subscription rather than taking a per-transaction cut, and is racquet-only.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Negligible. 4 TR ratings. English-only listing.

competitors.name: Padel Manager / PadelMix / Americano Padel Manager
competitors.whatItDoes: Tournament-format tools for running Americano and Mexicano padel events — team pairing, scheduling, live web sharing of results. Not booking or matchmaking platforms.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Minimal. Touches the Play and Rate steps only inside an organised event; no LEVEL, no RELIABILITY, no discovery, no money split.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Padel Manager 0 TR ratings; PadelMix 12 TR ratings. Neither localised for Turkey.

competitors.name: HalıSaha+ (Halı Saha+, formerly SahaGol) — Parpali Yazılım
competitors.whatItDoes: Turkish football super-app: pitch discovery and booking, AI "Hızlı Maç Bul" quick-match placement, per-player cost split via iyzico, team/squad management, rent-a-goalkeeper, transfer market, tournaments and league automation, an in-app social feed ("Tribün"), a business panel for pitch operators, and an explicit "Güven Puanı" trust score exposing each player's attendance reliability.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Near-total. Overlaps RELIABILITY (Güven Puanı / katılım güvenilirliği), LEVEL (AI placement by performance score; 4-tier Başlangıç–Profesyonel selector), CREATE (host a game with level, slots, cost split), MONEY ("Herkes Kendi Öder", ₺3.500 ÷ 14 = ₺250, no markup, iyzico-backed — the payments step Avenza defers), VENUES (pitch pages with price/photos/reviews), BULLETIN (Tribün social feed), and the neighbourhood onboarding step (profile location chip "İstanbul · Adalar +38").

No attendance percentage or reliability badge on the profile.

Freemium — two match requests per week free, Premium for unlimited requests, featured profile, direct messaging and full history.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: LEVEL (outcome-derived ELO, stronger signal than Avenza's self-declared 1.0–7.0), RATE (score submission after each match), CREATE (create a match with date/time/court), and it is the proof that subscription monetisation works in Turkish sports-social without taking a cut of the court split.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Turkish company, TR App Store since 2022-07-27, 4.25, n=271, v2.16.0 — the longest-running and best-rated-by-volume Turkish level-matching app found.

competitors.overlapWithAvenza: ELIGIBILITY ("Set the skill range" on match creation — Avenza's mechanic verbatim), LEVEL (ELO), CREATE, VENUES (court discovery with real hourly prices). Its browse-before-signup default is a direct counter to Avenza's deferred-signup-plus-hidden-games combination.

Ships "Built-in reputation system ensures reliable attendance", player profiles with skill ratings, selfie verification, private games and in-app messaging.

Notably has NO reliability or attendance mechanic and NO post-match rating — and has not shipped an update since 2022-06-29 despite being the highest-rating-count Turkish halı saha social app (4.60, n=154), which is the clearest available signal that a matching-only product without a trust loop stalls.

competitors.overlapWithAvenza: RATE and RELIABILITY — a two-way post-game rating explicitly framed as producing "güvenilir oyuncular" (trustworthy players) — plus level-band matching. A second Turkish entrant staking the trust position in the same launch window as Avenza.

competitors.name: Adam Eksik
competitors.whatItDoes: Single-purpose Turkish app for filling the last slot in a halı saha squad: post an ad or declare yourself available, filtered by il/ilçe/mahalle, FIFA-style player card with optional AI card photo, teams and challenges, chat on acceptance. competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Discover→Join at neighbourhood granularity (finer than Avenza's neighbourhood+radius), and a direct counterpoint to Avenza's MONEY mechanic by refusing commission entirely. Its existence — alongside "Eksik Adam", "Adam Eksik Mi" and "Dördüncü Eksik" in the same TR search results — shows the missing-player problem is named in Turkish app titles.

competitors.name: HalıSaha+ (Rezervasyon, Kadro) — formerly SahaGol
competitors.whatItDoes: Turkish football super-app already shipping, in production, almost the entire Avenza stack: AI matching on position/level/district ('Yapay zekâ seni performans puanına ve oyun sertliğine göre en dengeli maça yerleştirir'), a named trust score — 'GÜVEN PUANI — MAÇ İPTALİ DERDİ BİTSİN... Halı Saha+ Güven Puanı, maçı satıp ekibi yarı yolda bırakanları filtreler. Her oyuncunun katılım güvenilirliği profilinde görünür' — per-person split payment through a licensed PSP ('iyzico ile kredi kartı veya havale/EFT — herkes kendi payını öder'), post-match player rating, waitlist squad completion, rentable goalkeepers/players, venue-side booking automation with dynamic pricing, tournaments and leagues with online fee collection. v1.1.6, first released 8 May 2026, last updated 31 Aug 2026, 18 ratings at 4.33.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Near-total, and specifically on the two things Avenza calls its differentiator and its unsolved problem. It contradicts the brief's stated bet ('Nobody else knows whether the stranger you matched with will actually turn up, or is really the level they claim') — Güven Puanı is exactly a RELIABILITY attendance score and the AI matcher is exactly LEVEL matching. It also proves out the MONEY architecture from finding 1: an app on the Turkish App Store is doing per-player split collection via iyzico today, so the 'probably a licence' worry is answerable by copying a live production pattern. What it does NOT have is Avenza's ELIGIBILITY hard-filter (games outside your band hidden entirely), the multi-sport spread beyond football, or the BULLETIN feed.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Turkish-only, Turkey-first. Seller: Parpali Yazilim ve Bilisim Hizmetleri Ticaret Limited Sirketi. Site halisahaplus.com. Verified via itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=6761794919&country=tr.

competitors.name: Playtomic
competitors.whatItDoes: Padel/racket-sport court booking plus public and private match creation, level-based matching, cost splitting between players, leagues and tournaments, and a Premium tier that removes booking fees and adds 'Gold Match' promotion. Claims 'over 1 million players' and 'over 16,000 courts worldwide' in its own App Store copy.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Near-total on the core loop: DISCOVER/JOIN (public matches you can join), CREATE (host a match, set it public or private), MONEY (split the court fee between players), and LEVEL (level-based player recommendations). The one place it does NOT overlap is BULLETIN — no editorial feed anywhere in its listing. On ONBOARDING it is the direct counter-example: Playtomic demands a verified phone number on top of Apple/Google/Facebook/email sign-in, where Avenza has no phone or password field at all.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Live in the Turkish App Store: 188 TR ratings, 4.88 average, v6.88.0 released 31 Aug 2026. Localised presence confirmed via the country=tr iTunes lookup; TR court inventory not verified.

competitors.name: Kort (Kort: Find Tennis Partners)
competitors.whatItDoes: Tennis partner finder built by a Turkish company. Profile carries experience level and location; 'advanced algorithms' produce personalised matches; open invitations at a specific location and time that others can join; in-app messaging; Kort Challenge for recording results and tracking progress; Premium unlocks a coach/partner profile, location changing, notification broadcast of your open invites, and unlimited member discovery.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Direct on LEVEL (self-declared experience level driving matching), DISCOVER/JOIN (open invitations at a venue and time), and CREATE. Notably it monetises discovery limits via Premium rather than taking a cut of court cost, which is a different answer to MONEY than Avenza's 10% player-share fee. It has recorded results and progress tracking but no attendance/RELIABILITY score — the trust gap Avenza claims is real here. No editorial feed.
competitors.turkeyPresence: Turkish company (Distant Teknoloji Limited Şirketi, kortsports.com). Highest-rated direct competitor found in the TR store: 549 ratings at 4.83, v3.7.6 released 15 Jan 2026.

competitors.name: GoodRec
competitors.whatItDoes: On-demand pickup games (soccer, volleyball, basketball) in US cities — you pick a city and sport, join a game near you, see who is playing, invite friends, meet the host. Public per-city, per-sport web pages list upcoming games.
competitors.overlapWithAvenza: Same core loop and the closest match to Avenza's ONBOARDING bet. Its city pages are fully public — venue, date, time and duration render with no account — and the account wall sits on the JOIN action ('JOIN VIA APP'), which is exactly Avenza's deferred-signup pattern executed on the web as an SEO surface as well. Prices, spots left, skill level and host name are NOT shown publicly, so it gates the trust and money details, not the discovery.
